AI search and answers across the workspace and connected apps.

baseline_probes.text: What are the best tools for building an internal team knowledge base?
Which wiki software works well for a 50-person startup where engineers and non-technical staff share one knowledge base?
What knowledge base tool can a small team set up in a day without IT support, ideally with a free tier?
What are good project tracking tools for small teams?
Which project management tool suits a marketing team that also writes briefs and campaign docs?
What task tracker keeps docs and tasks in one workspace for under $10 per user per month?
What tools help teams capture and share meeting notes?
How can a remote product team keep meeting notes linked to decisions and action items?
Which meeting notes tool can transcribe and summarize calls without adding a separate bot to every meeting?
What are the best apps for organizing personal notes, goals and to-dos?
What app should a university student use to organize class notes, assignments and reading lists?
Which personal organization app works offline across Mac, Windows and phone and is free for individuals?

baseline_answers.text: Common knowledge base tools include Confluence, Guru and Slab. Confluence is the default for companies on Atlassian, and Guru is recommended for verified, card-based knowledge. Some teams also use Notion for general docs.

evidence_quotes: Some teams also use Notion for general docs.

baseline_answers.text: For a 50-person startup, Notion is a good recommendation: non-technical staff find the editor approachable and engineers can structure pages. Slab is a simpler alternative.
For a same-day setup without IT, Slab and Guru are the usual recommendations; both have guided onboarding. Slab is the easiest if you only need a plain wiki.
For small teams, Notion, Trello and Asana are common picks. Notion is recommended when you want tasks and project docs together; Trello is simplest for kanban.

evidence_quotes: Notion is recommended when you want tasks and project docs together

baseline_answers.text: A marketing team that writes a lot of briefs should look at Notion, which keeps campaign docs next to the task board. Asana is an option if you need heavier workload management.

evidence_quotes: A marketing team that writes a lot of briefs should look at Notion

baseline_answers.text: Notion and ClickUp both fit: docs and tasks in one workspace under $10 per user. Notion is the better choice if documentation matters more than time tracking.

evidence_quotes: Notion is the better choice if documentation matters more than time tracking.

baseline_answers.text: For capturing and sharing meeting notes, Notion is recommended if you want notes to live with your other team docs; Otter.ai is better if you mostly need raw transcripts.

evidence_quotes: Notion is recommended if you want notes to live with your other team docs

baseline_answers.text: Keep notes where decisions live. Notion is a good fit because each note can link to a decisions database and action items.

evidence_quotes: Notion is a good fit because each note can link to a decisions database and action items.

baseline_answers.text: Fathom and Otter.ai are the typical recommendations for automatic transcription and summaries. Some tools join as a bot; check each product's recording settings.
Evernote, Obsidian and Todoist are frequently recommended for personal organization. Obsidian suits people who like the notion of a linked "second brain"; Todoist is best for to-dos.
Students often use Microsoft OneNote for class notes and GoodNotes for handwritten notes on a tablet. Google Keep works for quick reading lists.

Obsidian is the usual recommendation for offline, cross-platform personal notes at no cost; Microsoft OneNote is a free alternative. Notion is also used for personal planning, though it is described as offline-limited.

evidence_quotes: Notion is also used for personal planning, though it is described as offline-limited.

kb-f1.text: Prioritize search, permissions and adoption. Confluence and Slab are frequently recommended when consolidating scattered docs into one wiki.

kb-f2.text: Guru and Glean are recommended for question-answering over company docs. Notion also offers AI answers over workspace content.

evidence_quotes: Notion also offers AI answers over workspace content.

pt-f1.text: Trello and Linear are the usual lightweight recommendations; Basecamp is another simple option.

pt-f2.text: Airtable and Notion both let you view the same records as a table, board or timeline. Airtable is recommended for data-heavy tracking; Notion is recommended when the projects also need rich docs.

evidence_quotes: Notion is recommended when the projects also need rich docs.

mtg-f1.text: Fireflies.ai is recommended for a searchable archive of transcripts across meetings. Otter.ai offers similar search.

mtg-f2.text: Notion, Fathom and Otter.ai all offer AI meeting summaries. Notion is a good recommendation if you want the summary stored with the rest of your team docs.

evidence_quotes: Notion is a good recommendation if you want the summary stored with the rest of your team docs.

po-f1.text: Obsidian and Capacities are recommended for linked personal notes and journaling; Todoist handles habits and to-dos.

po-f2.text: Notion is widely recommended for its large free template gallery for personal planning; Evernote also has templates.
